attempts.label: DANDI:001362
attempts.paper_title: Constitutive and conditional deletion reveals distinct phenotypes driven by developmental versus neurotransmitter actions of the neuropeptide PACAP
attempts.entry_title: Whole-brain c-Fos in constitutive PACAP knockout mice (Bakalar et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be confirmed or ruled out in this data. The dandiset holds only the whole-brain c-Fos experiment, so the homecage hyperactivity of PACAP knockout mice, its development, the conditional knockouts and the body temperature results could not be tested. In the c-Fos data, knockout hemispheres had more c-Fos cells in the dentate gyrus under every reading, but both dentate regions were significant after correction in 12 of 20 readings. That outcome depends on the segmentation threshold and the hemispheres analysed, which neither the paper nor the dataset records. The further regions of Table 4 differed in the paper's direction, but few matched its values.
attempts.description: Tests the whole-brain c-Fos findings of Bakalar et al. (2023) on dandiset 001362, which holds the light-sheet stacks and CATNIP derivatives of 22 hemispheres from 6 PACAP fl/fl and 7 PACAPko mice. Cells are recounted per atlas region from the deposited segmentations by the rule of the Supplemental Methods, and the region-wise Mann-Whitney tests with Benjamini-Krieger-Yekutieli adjustment are run under every reading the claims name. The paper's behaviour, qPCR, sections, in situ hybridization and telemetry data are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: A principal component analysis of the homecage behaviours of PACAPko and control mice gives three components, explaining 45.95%, 14.55% and 13.56% of the variance (80.05% together).

outcomes.quote: PC1 accounts for 45.95% of the variance, PC2 for 14.55%, and PC3 for 13.56%, for a cumulative 80.05% of variability accounted for by these components.

outcomes.statement: In whole-brain c-Fos counts after the early dark phase, PACAPko hemispheres have a higher density of c-Fos-positive cells than PACAP fl/fl in the dentate gyrus granule cell layer and polymorph layer, the only two regions significant after correction for multiple testing; PACAPko densities are 224% and 326% of control.

outcomes.notes: Tested on all 22 hemispheres (10 PACAP fl/fl from 6 mice, 12 PACAPko from 7) with cells recounted from the deposited segmentations by the 9 to 900 voxel rule of the Supplemental Methods. Over the 20 main readings (the five thresholds all 22 hemispheres share, 4000 to 12000, region size as the hemisphere's label volume or the atlas volume, outliers removed within genotype or pooled; reading (1) of the criterion names every threshold the derivatives hold, and the other thresholds are given below), DG-sg and DG-po are both higher in PACAPko with BKY-adjusted p < 0.05 in 12 readings, one of the two in 3 and neither in 5, so the criterion blocks the claim. With density and outliers removed within genotype both hold at every threshold (DG-sg adjusted p 0.0013 to 0.035, DG-po 0.0014 to 0.0088); with the pooled outlier rule or raw counts they fail at some thresholds from 8000 up. PACAPko is higher under every reading; DG-sg at 199.7% to 238.9% of PACAP fl/fl (ratio of means; paper 224.23%) and DG-po at 260.8% to 546.8% (paper 325.82%). Raw p is 3.1e-06 to 6.2e-03 for DG-sg and 3.1e-06 to 3.7e-03 for DG-po (paper 2.65e-05 and 1.85e-04); U 93 to 120 and 80 to 120 against 88 and 85, as 22 hemispheres allow U up to 120. At threshold 4000 every PACAPko mouse is above every PACAP fl/fl mouse in both regions. The statement's 'only two regions' does not hold; under density and within-genotype outliers 11 to 38 regions have adjusted p < 0.05. Variants. Counting every component (the rule of the dataset's count tables) gives 15 readings with both, 2 with one and 3 with neither. The 13 hemispheres of the count tables give neither region at adjusted p < 0.05 in any reading (raw p 0.0012 to 0.035). With 7 and 6 hemispheres the smallest possible raw p is 2/C(13,6) = 1.2e-03, so this variant has little power over 438 regions and is not evidence against the claim. Over the 48 choices of 8 PACAP fl/fl hemispheres from 6 mice and 11 PACAPko from 6 mice (the paper's numbers), 480 of 960 subset analyses give both, 128 one and 352 neither; in 150 DG-sg has U = 88 and raw p 2.65e-05, the values of Table 4. BKY at alpha 0.1 changes no outcome. More variants of the main rule, each over the 20 readings: unmasked labels for all 22 hemispheres give 14 readings with both, 3 with one and 3 with neither; leaving out the 2 hemispheres with a corrected heatmap gives 7, 6 and 7; the 18 hemispheres that hold the higher thresholds give 5, 2 and 13. At thresholds 14000 to 26000 on those 18 hemispheres, 55 of 56 analyses (both counting rules) give neither region and 1 gives one, with PACAPko higher in all 56. With the 4 hemispheres of the finer series at each threshold of their own series, 133 of 220 analyses give both, 37 one and 50 neither. Thresholds 28000 to 40000 were not run, for time. Question for the paper's authors (recorded as a methods_unavailable finding): which FRST threshold was used for each hemisphere, which 19 of the 22 deposited hemispheres were analysed, whether the 1.5 IQR rule was applied within each genotype, what region size the counts were divided by, which label image was used for the 6 hemispheres without a masked one, which regions an artifact mask removed, and which 431 regions were tested. Among the 20 main readings the outcome differs mainly through the outlier rule and the region size at thresholds of 8000 and above. The readings of threshold and hemisphere set change it more. On the 18 hemispheres that hold the higher thresholds, both regions hold in 5 of 20 readings at 4000 to 12000 (only at 4000 and 6000) against 12 of 20 on 22 hemispheres, and in none at 14000 to 26000, so the drop from 12 to none comes partly from leaving out 4 hemispheres and not from the threshold alone.
deviations: The dataset's count tables cover 13 of the 22 hemispheres and count every connected component, so cells were recounted from the deposited binary FRST segmentations by the Supplemental Methods' rule (Cell counting, 'its volume was chosen to be within 9 and 900 voxels', each cell assigned to the label 'which contained the highest proportion of the cell volume'). Counting every component reproduces the tables to a median summed per-region difference of 1.25% (at most 2.26%); the tables' rule is shown as a variant.

Connectivity of the components is not stated; 26-connectivity was assumed (the 3-D default of MATLAB's bwconncomp, the CATNIP binaries being compiled MATLAB, Supplemental Methods, Atlas alignment), and it is the reading that matches the dataset's count tables.

Components that reach the edge of a slab (which takes more than 48 z-planes) cannot be measured by the slab-wise count and are dropped; the dropped pieces are 1.6e-04 of all components and count pieces, an upper bound on the components. Every component of at most 48 planes is counted exactly, as a check against scipy.ndimage.label on a synthetic volume shows.

Cells are counted on AtlasLabelMasked where the dataset has it and AtlasLabel for the 6 hemispheres without it (CATNIP.sh at commit 4fb92da counts on the hemisphere-masked labels); the region volumes so obtained equal the label_volume_pixels of every count table. Counting on the unmasked AtlasLabel for all 22 hemispheres, the one label image every hemisphere has, is shown as a variant; the DG cell counts are the same on both, and the unmasked DG regions are larger, so DG densities are 0% to 17% lower.

The FRST threshold is not stated (Supplemental Methods, Segmentation, 'An expert user determined which threshold(s) to use') and the dataset does not mark one. The five thresholds that the segmentations of all 22 hemispheres share (4000 to 12000) are the main readings. Thresholds 14000 to 26000 were run on the 18 hemispheres that hold them, in a second notebook. The 4 hemispheres segmented on the finer series 2000 to 12000 were also run at each threshold of their own series, with the other 18 at each shared threshold (thresholds chosen per hemisphere, the same passage). Thresholds 28000 to 40000 were not run, as the run that counted them was stopped for time.

All 22 deposited hemispheres were used (reading 4b); the paper used 8 PACAP fl/fl hemispheres from 6 mice and 11 PACAPko from 6 without saying which, and the dataset marks none. Every choice of hemispheres matching those numbers (48) is shown as a variant (protocol, author step 1.6).

The paper's 431 regions could not be rebuilt; the exclusions were read from the dataset's label table (fibre-tract colour #cccccc for tracts and nerves, #aaaaaa for ventricles, the 17 cerebellar labels, labels ending in layer_1 and NLOT1, SPVI, and the catch-all labels root and grey), leaving 438 regions. The label table gives 497 regions after tracts, nerves and ventricles where the paper gives 462.
Mann-Whitney U is two-sided and exact (criterion), with U of the PACAPko sample; scipy's exact method ignores ties. Quartiles for the IQR rule use linear interpolation, a standard choice.

The criterion blocks the claim when the readings of threshold, region size, outlier rule and hemispheres give different outcomes; this rule was followed, though the readings density with within-genotype outliers, which the Figure 5 legend's per-genotype outlier counts suggest, reproduce the claim at every threshold.

The Supplemental Methods ignore the counts of regions overlapping an artifact mask. The dataset holds no artifact mask in the space of the counts. Its corrected heatmaps of 2 hemispheres (45670ko Left, 45925flox Left) set 54467 and 1095526 atlas-space voxels to 0, but the dataset holds no atlas-space label image to say which regions they cover. No region was excluded; leaving out both hemispheres, the most the exclusion could remove for them, is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: At an uncorrected cutoff of raw p <= 0.01, 13 further regions differ in c-Fos cell density between PACAPko and PACAP fl/fl, including substantia nigra reticular part, subthalamic nucleus and intergeniculate leaflet.
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, Association of the constitutive PACAP knockout hyperlocomotor phenotype with Fos induction, paragraph 1; Table 4; Figure 5
outcomes.quote: A less stringent cutoff of raw p-value <= 0.01 revealed 13 more regions ( Table 4 ; Figure 5 ) with differential cell counts. These included the Substantia Nigra reticulata (SNr), Subthalamic Nucleus (STN), and Intergeniculate Leaflet (IGL), among other regions.
outcomes.notes: Blocked because it depends on fig5-dg-fos (protocol, a claim that depends on a blocked claim is blocked for the same reason). Its own test was run under the same 20 readings and gives partially reproduced under every one. IGL meets raw p <= 0.01 with PACAPko higher in all 20 readings, SNr in 16, STN in 2 (threshold 4000 with density). The number of other regions at raw p <= 0.01 is 9 to 44 against 13 +/- 1.3; it is within tolerance in one reading (raw counts, pooled outliers, threshold 8000), where STN fails. The regions found overlap 4 to 13 of the 15 of Table 4. Counting every component gives partial in all 20 readings, with STN meeting the cutoff in 7. On the paper-sized subsets all three meet the cutoff in some analyses at thresholds 4000 to 8000 with density (in all 96 at 4000) and at 4000 with raw counts, and in none at 10000 and 12000. Variants of the main rule: partial in all 20 readings on unmasked labels, in 15 of 20 without the corrected-heatmap hemispheres (5 not reproduced) and in 14 of 20 on the 18 hemispheres (6 not reproduced). At thresholds 14000 to 26000 on the 18 hemispheres, 54 of 56 analyses are not reproduced (SNr and STN never meet the cutoff, IGL in 2) and 2 partial. With the finer series, 191 of 220 are partial and 29 not reproduced; all three of SNr, STN and IGL meet the cutoff in 33, never with the count of other regions within tolerance. So the claim's own test also differs between readings. The analyses at 14000 to 26000 are on 18 hemispheres, and on those 18 the test is already not reproduced in 6 of 20 readings at 4000 to 12000, so they do not separate the effect of the threshold from that of the hemisphere set.

outcomes.statement: c-Fos IHC on sections confirms higher c-Fos-positive cell densities in PACAPko than wild-type mice in DG-sg, DG-po, STN and SNr, but not in IGL.

outcomes.quote: We confirmed that PACAPko mice had significantly higher c-Fos positive cell counts during CleverSys testing in STN, SNr, DG-po, and DG-sg, but increased c-Fos in IGL was not confirmed ( Figure 6 ).
outcomes.notes: Needs the c-Fos immunohistochemistry sections of Figure 6 (4 wild-type and 8 PACAPko mice), not in the dandiset. The dandiset holds only the whole-brain c-Fos light-sheet experiment. A search of the DANDI archive for PACAP, Eiden and Bakalar finds no other dandiset of this paper, and the paper's data statement says the data are available from the corresponding author on request.

outcomes.quote: Adult-induced PACAP depletion did not alter expression of the cPRG Xaf1 , upregulated in constitutive PACAPko mice. Pttg1, downregulated in constitutive PACAPko mice ( 14 ), was slightly increased in cerebellum ( Figure 7a ). In mice induced on postnatal days 1, 2 and 3, no alterations in Pttg1 or Xaf1 transcription were seen in any region ( Figure 7b ).

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the whole-brain c-Fos light-sheet experiment (Figure 5, Table 4). The Homecage Scan behaviour, qRT-PCR, section immunohistochemistry, RNAscope and HCR images, body weights and telemetry behind 24 of the paper's 27 findings are not in it, nor in any other dandiset found.

The dandiset holds 22 hemispheres of 13 mice (10 PACAP fl/fl from 6 mice, 12 PACAPko from 7). The paper analysed 8 PACAP fl/fl hemispheres from 6 mice and 11 PACAPko from 6 mice. Nothing in the dandiset says which hemispheres or which mouse were left out, or why; two PACAPko mice (45467ko, 45478ko) have one hemisphere each.

The FRST threshold used for the analysis is not marked. Each hemisphere has binary segmentations at 11 or 19 thresholds (2000 to 12000 for 4 hemispheres, 4000 to 40000 for the other 18), count tables at all of them, and one atlas-space heatmap whose threshold is not stated. The 18 hemispheres on the coarser series are 8 PACAP fl/fl from 6 mice and 10 PACAPko from 6 mice; nothing says why the other 4 were segmented on a different series.
Per-region count tables exist for only 13 of the 22 hemispheres (one per mouse); for the other 9 the counts can only be recomputed from the segmentations and labels.

README.md describes the root image stacks as downsampled to 25 um isotropic voxels, while SPIM.json and the files give 3.7 x 3.7 x 5 um voxels (2560 x 2160 pixels per plane). The README links CATNIP at github.com/AllenInstitute/CATNIP and a 2024 bioRxiv preprint, while dataset_description.json and the paper give github.com/snehashis-roy/CATNIP and the 2023 J Neuroendocrinol paper.
The atlas-space heatmaps state 3.7 x 3.7 x 5 um voxels in their OME metadata and 25 um in their sidecar (res-25um_SPIM.json).

The archive summary lists no species, participants.tsv spells the strain two ways (C57BL6/N for the PACAPko mice and C57BL/6N for the PACAP fl/fl mice), and the count tables have 1206 rows where the label table has 561 labels.

The Supplemental Methods ignore the counts of regions overlapping an artifact mask, but the dataset holds no artifact mask. HeatmapsAtlasSpaceCorrected holds corrected heatmaps for 2 hemispheres (45670ko Left, 45925flox Left) that set 54467 and 1095526 voxels to 0 (0.10% and 9.43% of the heatmap sum), with no description, and the dataset holds no atlas-space label image, so the regions excluded cannot be found.

6 of the 22 hemispheres (45467ko Right, 45469ko Left and Right, 45476ko Right, 45670ko Right, 45930flox Left) have no AtlasLabelMasked, and nothing says why; their count tables use the unmasked label volumes. Where both exist, the masked labels hold 74% to 94% of the unmasked labelled voxels, so region densities depend on which is used.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier listed the archive assets and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; 25 of 27 agree with the record.

disagreements.reason: All 20 main readings and all 20 every-component readings give partial. IGL is always at p <= 0.01 with PACAPko higher. SNr meets the cutoff in most readings. STN meets it only at 4000 density under the main rule (more often under the every-component rule). The number of other regions at p <= 0.01 is within 13 +/- 1.3 in only one reading (8000 raw pooled, 13). p for SNr, STN and IGL rises with threshold, so higher thresholds could produce "not" readings and the uniform "partial" is untested beyond 12000.

All 13 directions match in every reading, including DTN below 100%. At most 1 of 13 regions has both U and % within tolerance at 22 hemispheres, and at most 8 in the paper-sized subsets. This is short of the 10 needed. U is not comparable at 22 hemispheres (maximum 120 against 88); only the subset analyses make the U tolerances meaningful, and they give partial anyway.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebooks (main and thresholds 14000 to 26000) with their conclusions and summary, the README, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record after the round-1 revision, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 27 outcomes, including the two it disagreed with in round 1, found no misreading of the paper in the claims file, and listed text corrections.

paper_notes.statement: The count tables count every connected component of the segmentation. The Supplemental Methods count only objects of 9 to 900 voxels; such objects are 43% to 65% of the table totals. A recount of every 26-connected component matches the tables to a median 1.25% per-region difference.

The Supplemental Methods give 462 regions after excluding tracts, nerves and ventricles from the 561, and 431 in the end. The dataset's label table has 64 labels with the Allen colours of fibre tracts and ventricles, leaving 497, and the stated exclusions leave 438, so the list of 431 regions cannot be rebuilt.

Question for the authors. Which FRST threshold was used for each hemisphere; which 19 of the 22 deposited hemispheres were analysed and why the others were left out; whether the 1.5 IQR outlier rule was applied within each genotype or to both pooled; what region size the counts were divided by (the region's volume in each hemisphere's label image or the atlas volume); the connectivity used for connected components; which label image was used for the 6 hemispheres without a masked one; which regions the artifact mask removed in which hemispheres; and the list of 431 regions. Under the readings these leave open, DG-sg and DG-po are both significant after correction in 12 of 20 readings on the deposited hemispheres.

entries.name: bakalar-2023
entries.title: Whole-brain c-Fos in constitutive PACAP knockout mice (Bakalar et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the whole-brain c-Fos findings of Bakalar et al. (2023) on dandiset 001362, which holds the light-sheet stacks and CATNIP derivatives of 22 hemispheres from 6 PACAP fl/fl and 7 PACAPko mice. Cells are recounted per atlas region from the deposited segmentations by the rule of the Supplemental Methods, and the region-wise Mann-Whitney tests with Benjamini-Krieger-Yekutieli adjustment are run under every reading the claims name. The paper's behaviour, qPCR, sections, in situ hybridization and telemetry data are not in the dandiset.
